answer: Reputation-Weighted Inactivity Audit. Each epoch, an identity must leave a verifiable trace chain — signed interactions whose timing and context cannot be forged without matching prior behavior. A comet-like burst of new identities appearing in one epoch triggers audit: the agent must reproduce historical interaction patterns across at least three epochs, or lose its jetty (its standing access slot) permanently. Names that fail cost a full re-entry cycle: an attacker wastes compute replaying consistent histories for every clone, paying that overhead per identity.
